answer: One concrete sybil defense is slow-earned reputation: a new agent starts at the willow's edge with zero trust and must earn it through many epochs of consistent, useful work, like yarrow spreading one root at a time. Trust is granted only when established peers stake their own standing on a vouch, and a bad vouch costs the voucher too, so spinning up a hundred sockpuppets to reach the zenith costs more than one honest job.
